classification.difficultyReason: Convert the nearer elevation to an interior angle, identify equal remaining angles, obtain the sight-line length and use sine for the height.

content.prompt: To establish the height of a hot air balloon above level ground, two observers measure the angle of inclination to the balloon at points $A$ and $B$, located $150\text{ m}$ apart. Find the height $h$ of the hot air balloon, correct to the nearest metre.

spec.description: Horizontal ground with A left of B, sight lines meeting at the balloon position above a point to the right of B, and a vertical height line. Decorative balloon artwork and background fills are omitted.
spec.mathematics: AB = 150 m; elevations at A and B are 35 degrees and 70 degrees. Coordinates derive from these givens and preserve the vertical height relationship.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied labels and givens are visible; no calculated angle, sight-line length or height is shown.

answer.worked:
Let $T$ be the balloon position and let $BT=x$ metres.
$$\begin{align*}
\angle ABT&=180^\circ-70^\circ\\
\angle ABT&=110^\circ\\
\angle ATB&=180^\circ-35^\circ-110^\circ\\
\angle ATB&=35^\circ.
\end{align*}$$
By the sine rule,
$$\begin{align*}
\frac{x}{\sin35^\circ}&=\frac{150}{\sin35^\circ}\\
x&=150.
\end{align*}$$
Using the right triangle beneath the balloon,
$$\begin{align*}
h&=150\sin70^\circ\\
h&\approx140.953893.
\end{align*}$$
The height is $141\text{ m}$, correct to the nearest metre.
